finding: A0 is recorded complete, but its registered architecture-bundle test hashes raw checkout bytes. On a Windows CRLF checkout it fails while ReleaseLedger's canonical LF hash audit passes. A0 therefore does not mechanically prove its required portable_canonical_hashes check across supported checkouts.

evidence.observation: The test calls read_bytes() and hashlib.sha256() directly instead of the canonical text hash policy used by ReleaseLedger.

evidence.failure: The two architecture documents have CRLF-sensitive raw-byte digests on this checkout.

evidence.observation: The controller correctly validates the locked architecture bundle with canonical portable hashing.

root_cause: The A0 controller implementation was made portable, but one A0 mechanical acceptance assertion retained the earlier raw-byte hashing method. Its prior green result depended on checkout line endings.
required_control_action: Fail the active A1 claim without recording A1 completion.
Invalidate completed A0 so ReleaseLedger returns the owning work package.
Repair and revalidate A0 in its own work package before A1 can complete.

a1_working_state.note: A1 domain repairs remain uncommitted working state and must be revalidated after A0 is repaired.

downstream_observation.note: A2 generic SCRIPT_FACT mapping fixtures are correctly rejected by the repaired A1 authority. They remain A2-owned and were not modified.
